items.stem: Which best describes a well-formed user story?

options.text: As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit] - with clear acceptance criteria
options.rationale: Correct: a user story states role, need and benefit and is testable via acceptance criteria.
That is a design artefact, not a user story.
A user story captures a need from the user's perspective, not schema.
A contract is a commercial document, not a user story.

items.explanation: Correct: a user story states role, need and benefit and is testable via acceptance criteria.

items.stem: A stakeholder says 'add a button that creates a renewal record.' What should the BA do first?

options.text: Explore the underlying business need and problem being solved
options.rationale: Correct: the BA frames the problem before accepting a prescribed solution, ensuring the real need is met.
Jumping to a solution risks solving the wrong problem.
The request is input; the BA should understand the need, not dismiss it.
There is no legal issue indicated; discovery of the need comes first.

items.explanation: Correct: the BA frames the problem before accepting a prescribed solution, ensuring the real need is met.

items.stem: Which TWO are good uses of acceptance criteria?

options.text: They define when a story is done and testable
options.rationale: Correct: acceptance criteria set the conditions of satisfaction for a story.

options.text: They give UAT testers the basis for test cases
options.rationale: Correct: UAT test cases are derived from acceptance criteria.

options.text: They replace the need for any stakeholder involvement

options.rationale: Acceptance criteria describe behaviour, not infrastructure.

options.text: They are written only after go-live
options.rationale: They are defined before development, not after go-live.

items.explanation: Correct: acceptance criteria set the conditions of satisfaction for a story.
